static.title: Vetting a candidate
static.note: A dip that repeats is only a candidate. Three tests try to reject it: do odd and even transits have the same depth, is there a second eclipse half an orbit later, and is the light that dips at the target’s position. Each test says pass, fail or inconclusive, and inconclusive is an answer of its own: the data could not decide. A candidate that no test rejects is not validated. Every candidate here is synthetic: a model made it, and the truth can be shown.

samples.label: Candidate
samples.value: A: a clean dip: 14400 light-curve points every 3 minutes, 0.0400 percent noise per point, repeating every 3.2 d; 111 frames of a 17 by 17 pixel stamp

samples.label: Test 1: odd and even depths
samples.value: pass: the odd and even depths agree, and the test could have seen a difference. Depths 1.152 and 1.158 percent, difference −0.0059 ± 0.0053 percent (1.1 sigma); it could see a difference of 0.0160 percent, 1 percent of the depth

samples.label: Test 2: a second eclipse
samples.value: pass: no second eclipse, and the test could have seen a deep one. Depth at half an orbit later 0.0020 ± 0.0025 percent; it would have seen 0.0076 percent, 1 percent of the primary

samples.label: Test 3: where the light dips
samples.value: pass: the dip is at the target’s position, and a source beyond the exclusion radius would have shown. The dip is 0.08 pixels from the target (0.8 sigma); a source farther than 0.34 pixels would have shown

samples.label: Overall
samples.value: Not rejected: every test that ran passed. That is not validation: the tests rule out some false positives and leave others.

static.title: Verificar un candidato
static.note: Una caída que se repite es solo un candidato. Tres pruebas intentan rechazarlo: si los tránsitos impares y pares tienen la misma profundidad, si hay un segundo eclipse media órbita después, y si la luz que baja está en la posición del objetivo. Cada prueba dice aprobada, suspendida o no concluyente, y no concluyente es una respuesta propia: los datos no pudieron decidir. Un candidato que ninguna prueba rechaza no está validado. Todos los candidatos son sintéticos: los hizo un modelo, y se puede mostrar la verdad.

samples.label: Candidato
samples.value: A: una caída limpia: 14400 puntos de la curva de luz cada 3 minutos, 0.0400 por ciento de ruido por punto, con un período de 3.2 d; 111 imágenes de un recorte de 17 por 17 píxeles

samples.label: Prueba 1: profundidades impar y par
